The front ends have broad slanted trapezoidal faces continuing the paired opened collar posts; no spear tips. variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, very restrained redesign of the EXACT source spacecraft.
Create one concept sheet for the EXISTING Freelancer li_pir_elite (pirate Liberty elite). The owner rejected the previous ten wholesale redesigns. This time fidelity to this precise model is the highest priority: the original long POLYGONAL BLOCK body, compact proportions, front cabin, wing fans, two unequal vertically stacked aft engines, rear transverse spoiler, native painted surfaces and Art Deco identity remain immediately recognizable. Add only a few deliberate nuances following the owner's drawings. Not another ship, not a new layout.

REFERENCE ROLES IN ORDER:
1. Exact immutable original cockpit, multiple views: copy its shell shape, proportions, pane boundaries, thin existing frames and rounded glazed nose. It is not enlarged, stretched or replaced. No cut may enter the cabin shell or glazing.
2. Owner's FRONT markup on the actual source: BLUE marks two substantial LEFT/RIGHT raised tapering hull sides. Read this as an obelisk-like cross-section: two broad solid sides leaning gently inward as they rise, with an open recessed middle. They are portions of the hull, not two thin rails, an open frame or literal freestanding monuments.
3. Owner's PERSPECTIVE markup: the same two side masses run LONGITUDINALLY from behind the cabin collar to the rear spoiler, flanking the sunken cargo deck. This is the most important local geometry guide. GREEN marks REAL MATERIAL TO REMOVE from the EXTERNAL COLLAR at those marked positions. They are cutouts/notches, never green paint, windows or attachments. Remove the marked portions of the external flange rims, opening their outlines so that TWO broad parallel side posts are emphasized, then continue those posts into the raised longitudinal body sides. Make this paired-post rhythm stronger and wider. Keep the underlying cabin shell completely intact. The old continuous collar band should visibly have the requested interruptions. Blue and green are annotations only; neither color appears on the finished ship.
4. Actual original li_pir_elite in flight, front/rear/top/side: AUTHORITATIVE whole-ship shape, dimensions, materials, separate engine shapes, wing fans, aft spoiler and native surface-art vocabulary. Stay very close to it, including its warm worn red/ochre panels, pale incised fan motifs, darker recessed panels and modest metal trim. Do not import the heavy copper/gold trim, rectangular radiator engines or big furniture-like ornament of previous AI sheets.
5. Actual cargo doors closed/open: TWO longitudinal top leaves with a fore-aft center seam and outer long-edge hinges. Preserve this opening principle and keep the cargo area WITHIN the recessed center, between the new raised sides. The illustration is not mechanical clearance proof.

ONLY THREE CHANGES:
A. Raise and widen the TWO parallel solid hull sides from the blue markup, gently tapered inward like truncated obelisks. They remain full longitudinal shell masses, with broad native-style outer side panels. Keep the original lower multi-faceted block and its dimensions. Increase height modestly, not into towers. Between them, the cargo hatch/deck remains visibly LOWER, a recessed well: do NOT join the two pylons by a flush roof, fill the middle with a new spine, or move the hatch to their highest surface. Leave a visible clear central width and room for the paired doors to open. Keep the hatch itself a secondary feature in this well.
B. Cut the GREEN marked external collar segments, with real negative-space notches visible in the front and perspective views, strengthening two wider parallel side posts that align with the raised hull sides. Protect the entire cabin and its original interior. The notches remove flange material only; they do not become holes into a hollow cockpit.
C. Raise the original separate transverse REAR SPOILER a little ABOVE the two hull-side tops. Preserve its readable original span, solid downturned ends and connection to the stern. Develop its specific outline as described below. Retain the native two unequal polygonal/octagonal engine units below it in their original VERTICAL arrangement, original positions and scale, rather than replacing them.

Preserve the native THREE thin overlapping leaf wings on each side with their original forward pivot cluster, broad fan silhouette, patterned native surfaces and folding direction. The owner may explore fewer leaves later; in these two trials wing reduction is deliberately not introduced. No new wing architecture. Add modest shallow relief only where native surface artwork already suggests it: the fan/frieze side fields, a few narrow vertical flute strips on the paired posts and the original stern motif. Original li_pir_elite style comes before generic Empire decoration. No rods, exposed pipe bundles, giant sunburst plaques, repeated gold picture frames, tiny rivet geometry, cathedral details, statuary, extra nacelles or forked stern.

SHEET: quiet pale-grey background, clear production concept illustration of the original model with the limited modifications, strong large facets and moderate native-level detail. Main large FRONT-SIDE three-quarter flight view from slightly above, comparable to owner's perspective markup, showing BOTH raised sides and the recessed central deck. Nose to lower LEFT. This view must reveal the real collar notches. Supporting orthographic FRONT (essential: paired inward-tapering sides, intact cabin, interrupted collar, higher spoiler), SIDE and TOP nose UP. Include a small CARGO OPEN inset showing the same well and paired doors, with both raised side shells fixed. Keep the SAME exact ship and cockpit across all views. Text only concept ID, FRONT, SIDE, TOP, CARGO OPEN. No colored guide strokes. All drawings refer to ONE variant.

LOCAL VARIATION:
L45. The two widened hull-side obelisks have one clean LONG STRAIGHT rising upper edge each, gently rising toward the stern, with a narrow flat bevel-like crown made as a deliberate facet of the new form, not rounded smoothing. The front ends have broad slanted trapezoidal faces continuing the paired opened collar posts; no spear tips. Their outer surfaces preserve the original long sunburst/frieze fields at the original modest scale. The upper central roof remains a recessed channel. The raised original rear spoiler becomes a single broad horizontal cornice with a very shallow stepped central rise and original downward end returns. The spoiler is the highest element, but only slightly above the side pylons. Its lower edge remains visibly separate from the deck. Show actual removal at the green collar marks, not merely a dark painted rectangle.
Label L45.
variants.visual_review: Основной многоугольный брусок, родная окраска, мотивы, веер и поперечный спойлер узнаваемо сохранены. Две широкие приподнятые боковины образуют пониженный центральный канал, спойлер выше их верха. Верх воротника между боковыми стойками раскрыт; степень нижнего выреза у зелёной отметки в перспективе не доказана — потребуется уточнение на геометрии/крупном фронтальном виде. На CARGO OPEN показан трюм с открытой парой створок, однако это не проверка полной траектории и боковых зазоров. Кабина близка к источнику, но её точный контур нельзя брать с растра; исходный CMP обязателен.

variants.direction: L46. Preserve exactly the same source hull and two longitudinal side obelisks, but give each side a SMALL TWO-STEP upper silhouette and a wide sloped outer face, tapering inward toward its top. The paired front collar posts are broad with a restrained longitudinal recess, the green marked interruptions cutting cleanly through the flange rims. The two raised sides remain separate across a clearly lowered cargo well. The higher native rear spoiler keeps its transverse connected body and downturned ends, but its TOP has two squared raised shoulders aligned over the paired side masses, separated by a shallow angular central dip. This is a modest revised top contour of the original spoiler, not two separate towers or a large arch. Use native stern fan art in the lower central face and restrained shallow stepped/fluted relief on the two caps. Difference from L45 is the stepped side tops and the paired shoulders in the spoiler contour; the basic native ship remains the same.

variants.visual_review: Сохранены многоугольная основа, родные цветовые поля, рисунки веера и вертикальная пара исходных двигателей. Два приподнятых боковых пилона имеют небольшие уступы; над ними — связный поперечный спойлер с двумя поднятыми плечами и пониженным центром. Между пилонами остаётся утопленная площадка/трюм. Внешний воротник раскрыт сверху; после отдельной правки появились небольшие видимые нижние выкусы в контуре фланцев (особенно SIDE), без вырезания кабины. Точность границы относительно зелёной метки ещё требует исходной геометрии. TOP повёрнут носом влево вопреки тексту задания, но показывает требуемую схему. CARGO OPEN — замысел раскрытия, не валидация движения. Растр не заменяет оригинальный кокпит.
